gloss: to be thirsty; to get thirsty

definitions.gloss: to be thirsty; to get thirsty; to have a dry throat
definitions.explanation: The standard expression for feeling thirsty. Literally means 'the throat dries out.' This is the natural way to express thirst in Japanese, rather than using a single adjective.

examples.japanese: {運動|うんどう}した{後|あと}は{喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}く。
{喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}いたので、コンビニで{冷|つめ}たいお{茶|ちゃ}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I was thirsty, so I bought a cold tea at the convenience store.

notes:
The standard Japanese expression for being thirsty. Literally '{喉|のど} (throat) が (subject marker) {渇|かわ}く (to dry out).' Japanese expresses thirst through this phrase rather than a single adjective. The past form {喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}いた is very common in conversation to say 'I'm thirsty.'

USAGE:
The kanji {渇|かわ}く means to become parched or dry from lack of moisture. Note the difference from {乾|かわ}く (to dry, to become dry), which is used for objects like laundry.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}いた: I'm thirsty (past/resultative)
- {喉|のど}がカラカラに{渇|かわ}く: to be extremely thirsty (throat bone-dry)
- {喉|のど}の{渇|かわ}きを{潤|うるお}す: to quench one's thirst

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{腹|なか}が{空|す}く: to be hungry — the parallel expression for hunger
- {喉|のど}が{乾燥|かんそう}する: for the throat to be dry — medical/physical dryness, not thirst
